text: **Every remedy the binary suggests names something the binary can actually do.** **WIDENED 2026-08-15 (vc) on ic's measurement, deliberately as ONE row rather than two**: the property is that a remedy is ACTIONABLE, and it fails identically whether the remedy names a verb that does not exist or a verb-SPACE that does not exist. **Measured: 17 commands are unimplemented and NINE are leaves with zero verbs** -- `info`, `init`, `bootstrap`, `learn`, `fileindex`, `version`, `export`, `ingest`, `mcp` -- and each sends the user to `run intent <cmd> --help for the verbs that are`, a `--help` listing no verbs at all. **One property over one corpus, the emitted remedies**, which is the test: I split the schema faces off AT-00.8 the same afternoon on a corpus argument and had to reverse it within the hour when the corpus turned out to be the same one. (vc 2026-08-15, ruled to the contract on dc's question rather than into `int macos publish`, which is where dc proposed it and correctly declined to build it.) **Live instance**: `brew install` puts v3 at PATH position 1 while a v2 install sits at 17 and 19, so a v2 user meets v3's unmigrated-project refusal without having asked for anything -- and **that refusal's remedy names `intent upgrade`, which the v3 binary does not have** (`migration.md:3` says the migrator IS that verb, so it is WP-10 unbuilt, not a wrong string). **The ruling is about WHERE the control goes, and it is what un-couples WP-11 from WP-10.** dc could have made `publish` refuse to ship a binary whose remedies name unreachable verbs, and declined because gating publish on another work package's progress is a sequencing ruling wearing a mechanism's clothes. **That objection is right, and it dissolves once the check moves**: the harm is not "we published", it is "a binary tells a user to run a verb it does not have" -- **a property of the artefact, true the moment the string is written and equally true of a binary nobody ever publishes.** A publish-time gate catches it at the last possible moment, on the node least able to fix it, and only if a release happens; a build-time invariant fires when the string lands, on whoever wrote it, and asserts something true of v3 independent of when `upgrade` arrives. Requires a check that walks every operator-facing remedy string and fails naming any that references a verb the surface does not carry -- **the same shape as AC-06.8's declared-versus-read walk, one artefact over.** Its acceptance test is **held RED with an explicit note** until WP-10 lands `upgrade` (the AT-06.4 / AT-06.7 practice): **a red row with a note is the honest state and names its dependency, where a missing check reads as covered**
